assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full; driver_capability: ready
=> route: record

## Scenario

`turn-aborted-by-error` asserts the user-observable arc `ready -> working -> ready`: the model call fails mid-turn (network error, provider 5xx, timeout), the agent gives up, and the session must NOT stick in `working`. It is explicitly not the user-cancel path (`user-esc-interrupt`).

The load-bearing question for copilot was narrow and existential: irrlicht's ONLY route back to `ready` for this adapter is `assistant.turn_end` (`core/adapters/inbound/agents/copilot/parser.go`, `case evTurnEnd: ev.EventType = "turn_done"`). If an aborted turn emitted no `assistant.turn_end`, the session would stay `working` forever and this cell would be `daemon=bug` (a trace exists but is mis-handled) or `daemon=incapable` (no trace at all).

## agent_supports: yes — live-verified

Copilot CLI 1.0.77 aborts the turn after a bounded retry budget and reports it. Two independent live runs against a controlled endpoint (details under "How this was settled"):

- provider 5xx: 5 retries over 33.25s, then stderr `Failed to get response from the AI model; retried 5 times (total retry wait time: 33.25 seconds) Last error: 503 upstream overloaded`, exit code 1.
- unreachable endpoint: 5 retries over ~6.2s, then `Could not connect to local model provider at http://127.0.0.1:18766/v1.` In the interactive REPL the prompt box returned to `❯` — the session SURVIVES the abort and stays usable, which is what lets an interactive recipe observe the settled `ready` state instead of racing process teardown.

The code path is the agentic loop's own catch arm in the CLI bundle (`app.js`): `catch(c){ … this.emit("session.error", {errorType: … "query", message: `Execution failed: …`, statusCode: …}) } finally { … this.endNativeTurn(), this.mcpHost?.sendNotification("assistant.turn_end") … }` — the turn is ended on the error path, not left open.

## daemon_capability: full — the abort DOES write assistant.turn_end

The live transcript of the aborted turn (verbatim event order from `$COPILOT_HOME/session-state/<id>/events.jsonl`):

```
21:43:35.944  session.start
21:43:36.969  session.model_change
21:43:37.055  system.message
21:43:37.063  user.message           <- ready -> working
21:43:37.089  assistant.turn_start
21:44:10.483  assistant.turn_end     <- working -> ready  (THE ABORT)
21:44:10.498  session.error          {"errorType":"query","statusCode":503,"message":"Failed to get response … 503 upstream overloaded"}
21:44:10.543  session.shutdown
```

Note the ORDER: `assistant.turn_end` precedes `session.error`. There is no `assistant.message` on an aborted turn, so the settle is carried purely by the explicit turn boundary — exactly the signal the copilot parser already maps. No parser change is needed and no sweep is needed: recovery is event-driven, not timer-driven (there is no working-state idle sweep since PR #106 — `core/application/services/pid_manager.go` TTL-cleans only `StateReady` or PID-dead sessions).

The same shape was observed for the pure connect-refused failure, so the mapping is not specific to one error class.

Persistence is not inferred — it is schema-declared. `schemas/session-events.schema.json` in the CLI bundle marks transient events with `"ephemeral": {"const": true, "description": "Always true for events that are transient and not persisted to the session event log on disk"}`. `AssistantTurnEndEvent` and `ErrorEvent` (session.error) carry the plain non-const `ephemeral` property, i.e. they ARE persisted; `AssistantTurnRetryEvent`, `IdleEvent` (session.idle) and `ModelCallFailureEvent` are `const: true`, i.e. never written to disk. That is why the retry chatter and the idle signal are invisible on disk while the turn boundary and the error are not — and it matches the live capture exactly.

## driver_capability: ready

The recipe needs `send` + `wait_turn` + `sleep`. `replaydata/agents/copilot/driver-interactive.sh` line 128 declares `DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash sleep wait_turn exit_clean sigkill interrupt keys restart start_session session reset_session resume"` — all three are elicited. `wait_turn` counts `assistant.turn_end` occurrences, and the aborted turn emits one, so the driver's turn gate closes on the abort rather than hanging to the timeout.

No new driver primitive is required. The BYOK environment reaches the CLI the same way the existing copilot cells pass `COPILOT_AVAILABLE_TOOLS` / `COPILOT_NO_ALLOW_ALL`: the driver's `tmux new-session … copilot` inherits the driver process environment, so the variables are exported before driving and named in `prereqs` (the precedent is the 2-2 / 2-3 / 2-4 cells).

## How this was settled (and why it costs nothing)

`copilot help providers` documents BYOK: `COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` "API endpoint URL (required to activate BYOK)", plus `COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE` (openai default), `COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY`, `COPILOT_PROVIDER_WIRE_API`, and `COPILOT_MODEL`. Critically: "GitHub authentication is not required when using a custom provider." So a BYOK session never touches GitHub's CAPI and spends ZERO AI credits — the `session.shutdown` of the aborted probe reports `totalNanoAiu: 0, totalPremiumRequests: 0`.

That is what made this cell settleable without spending the maintainer's credits, and it is what makes it recordable deterministically: unlike the CAPI path, a BYOK endpoint can be made to fail on demand.

Three probes were run (all against `$COPILOT_HOME` under a scratch dir, never the real store):

1. Headless `copilot -p` with `COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` pointed at an always-503 OpenAI-compatible stub — produced the transcript quoted above.
2. Headless `copilot -p` against the committed `tools/onboarding-factory/recording/mock-openai-429` — the HAPPY path works end to end with copilot's BYOK wire (`assistant.message` with `outputTokens: 1`, `session.shutdown.modelMetrics` populated), confirming the rig's existing OpenAI mock speaks a wire format copilot accepts.
3. Interactive tmux `copilot --allow-all --no-color` with the base URL pointed at a dead port — same `assistant.turn_start -> assistant.turn_end -> session.error` shape, and the REPL stayed alive and accepted input afterwards.

## Why the recipe uses an unreachable endpoint rather than a mock process

Probe 1 and probe 3 produce the SAME observable transcript, so the cell is not tied to one error class. The recipe picks the unreachable endpoint because it is strictly more deterministic and has fewer moving parts:

- Every model call fails, so the cell cannot be invalidated by an extra completion request (a session-title call, a retry accounting differently) consuming a mock's happy-path budget. `mock-openai-429` streams a successful completion for request #1 and only fails from #2 on, which would make a single-turn recipe depend on copilot issuing exactly one request.
- No mock process to build, start, port-bind, or reap inside the recording rig — nothing to leak into a later cell.
- It is faster: ~6s to abort vs ~33s for the 5xx retry ladder.

"Network error" is the first failure mode the scenario's own description names, so this is an in-spec elicitation, not a proxy for one.

## Not conflated: a failed TOOL is not an aborted TURN

`tool.execution_complete.data.success == false` maps to `ParsedEvent.IsError` in the copilot parser. That is a tool-level failure inside a turn that continues; it is not this scenario and is not what the recipe elicits. This cell's abort produces no `tool.execution_complete` at all.
caveats: session.error IS persisted (schema: ErrorEvent has no const-true `ephemeral`) and carries errorType/message/statusCode, but the copilot parser has no arm for it — it falls to the default `ev.Skip = true`. The abort is therefore observable as a STATE arc but the error itself is not surfaced in the timeline. This is a caveat, not a bug: the scenario's acceptance criteria assert state topology only, and the spec-required observable (working -> ready) is fully produced. Surfacing session.error as an error event would be a small parser addition (a `default`-arm graduation, same shape as parseToolComplete's IsError), worth its own issue if the timeline should show WHY a turn ended.

The recording runs in BYOK mode, so the session's model is the BYOK model id, not a CAPI model, and cost/tokens are effectively absent: an aborted turn writes no assistant.message (so the live outputTokens path contributes nothing) and session.shutdown reports `modelMetrics: {}`. The observation vector therefore asserts NEITHER cost_nonzero NOR tokens_nonzero — verified from the probe's shutdown payload. The only token signal is `currentTokens` on session.shutdown, which lands at teardown and is deliberately not asserted.

model is deliberately NOT pinned in the observation vector. The BYOK model id is whatever COPILOT_MODEL is set to, and it passes through tailer.NormalizeModelName before reaching the websocket; record fills it from the recording rather than risking an exact-match failure on a normalisation this assessment did not verify.

The two-phase presession birth is templated from the copilot/basic-turn sibling and is PROVISIONAL for the same reason it is there: copilot creates session-state/<id>/ at launch but writes events.jsonl only on the first prompt, so a proc-<PID> row is expected first. That ordering was not re-verified for this cell; if record observes the real session born directly, it re-anchors the birth phases.

The abort was verified from copilot's own transcript, not through a live irrlichd. The parser mapping (assistant.turn_end -> turn_done) is direct and shared with the already-assessed basic-turn cell, so the daemon-side settle is a one-line inference from a verified trace — but it is record that promotes it from inferred to observed.

sources.note: case evTurnEnd: ev.EventType = "turn_done" is the adapter's ONLY route back to ready; session.error has no arm and falls to default ev.Skip = true; parseToolComplete's success==false -> IsError is a tool-level failure, not a turn abort.

Aborted-turn transcript: session.start, session.model_change, system.message, user.message, assistant.turn_start, assistant.turn_end (21:44:10.483), session.error {errorType:query, statusCode:503} (21:44:10.498), session.shutdown. turn_end precedes the error; no assistant.message on the aborted turn; shutdown reports modelMetrics:{} and totalNanoAiu:0.

AssistantTurnEndEvent and ErrorEvent(session.error) carry a plain `ephemeral` property = PERSISTED to events.jsonl; AssistantTurnRetryEvent, IdleEvent(session.idle) and ModelCallFailureEvent declare `ephemeral: {const: true, 'Always true for events that are transient and not persisted to the session event log on disk'}` = never written. Explains why retry chatter is invisible on disk while the turn boundary and the error are not.

Agentic-loop error arm: catch emits session.error {errorType: authentication|query, message: 'Execution failed: …', statusCode}; the finally arm runs endNativeTurn() and sends the assistant.turn_end notification — the turn is closed on the error path. (The bundled `copilot` binary is a compressed Node SEA and yields nothing to `strings`; app.js is the readable source of record.)

BYOK: COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL activates a custom provider; COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE openai|azure|anthropic; COPILOT_MODEL required. 'GitHub authentication is not required when using a custom provider' — so a BYOK recording spends ZERO AI credits (probe shutdown: totalNanoAiu 0, totalPremiumRequests 0) and is the deterministic error-injection seam copilot was assumed not to have.

Line 128 DRIVE_ELICITS includes send, wait_turn and sleep — the whole recipe. launch_repl runs `tmux new-session … copilot --allow-all --no-color`, inheriting the driver's environment, which is how the existing cells pass COPILOT_AVAILABLE_TOOLS / COPILOT_NO_ALLOW_ALL and how the BYOK variables reach the CLI. wait_turn counts assistant.turn_end, which the aborted turn emits, so the turn gate closes on the abort.

Probe 2: the committed OpenAI mock's happy path drives copilot's BYOK wire successfully (assistant.message outputTokens 1, modelMetrics populated). Kept as evidence that a mock-upstream variant is available, but NOT used by the recipe: request #1 is always the happy path, so a single-turn recipe would depend on copilot issuing exactly one completion request.

The PID-liveness sweep TTL-cleans only StateReady or PID-dead sessions, so there is no working-state idle sweep to fall back on. Recovery here is event-driven via assistant.turn_end — which is exactly why the emission question was existential for this cell.
Sibling spec this cell's presession two-phase birth and phase anchoring are templated from.

preconditions: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.77 on PATH. NO GitHub authentication is required and NO AI credits are spent: the cell runs in BYOK mode, which bypasses GitHub's CAPI entirely (`copilot help providers`; probe shutdown reported totalNanoAiu 0 / totalPremiumRequests 0).

Export the BYOK environment before driving — the driver's tmux launch inherits it, the same way the 2-2 / 2-3 / 2-4 cells pass COPILOT_AVAILABLE_TOOLS: COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18799/v1, COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE=openai, COPILOT_PROVIDER_WIRE_API=completions, COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY=sk-irrlicht-unused, COPILOT_MODEL=irrlicht-turn-abort-model.
NOTHING may be listening on 127.0.0.1:18799 — that is the whole error-injection mechanism. Every model call gets ECONNREFUSED, so the abort cannot be dodged by an extra completion request.
irrlichd is recording — run-cell.sh in isolated mode, or --attach against a daemon started with --record.
no other copilot session shares the same cwd (the PID is bound by cwd).
setup: The driver seeds a scratch COPILOT_HOME under the staging dir with trustedFolders + askedSetupTerminals pre-answered, so the trust modal cannot block the input box; the session directory is minted under $COPILOT_HOME/session-state/<session-id>/ and events.jsonl appears only on the first prompt.

Copilot prints a one-line banner warning that the BYOK model is not in the built-in catalog and it is falling back to default token limits. This is expected and does not block the input box (observed live).

The turn aborts after copilot's bounded retry ladder — ~6s for a refused connection (5 retries). The 120s floor is ample; 180 is set to absorb REPL startup plus the retry ladder if a slower failure mode (DNS/timeout rather than refusal) is ever substituted.

script.text: Reply with exactly the word: ok

verify: events.jsonl mints a proc-<PID> pre-session in ready shortly after launch (the copilot process exists before its events.jsonl does)
events.jsonl mints the real <session-id> session in ready under a DIFFERENT session id once events.jsonl appears on the first prompt
events.jsonl contains a pid_discovered binding the copilot PID to the real session (matched by cwd)
events.jsonl contains a state_transition to working on the real session when the user prompt lands

events.jsonl contains a state_transition to ready on the real session carried by the ABORT: copilot writes assistant.turn_end when it gives up (5 failed model calls), the parser maps it to turn_done, and IsAgentDone() fires — the session does NOT stick in working. Recovery is event-driven; there is no working-state sweep.
the settle is NOT carried by an assistant message — an aborted turn writes no assistant.message at all
events.jsonl never contains a state_transition to waiting (no tool call, so no permission.requested)
the session remains alive and ready through the trailing sleep (the REPL survives the abort — verified live), so the final state is observed on a live session rather than raced against teardown
final state of the real session is ready
observation vector: cost and tokens are deliberately NOT asserted (an aborted turn produces no assistant.message and session.shutdown reports modelMetrics:{}); model is left for record to fill
